title: Havenbrook FinServ quick intake & field notes
content:
Context:
- 2024-11-06 intake call with Havenbrook Product + Platform leads (see attendees). They want a conversational assistant for agent desktops + secure batch scoring for AML rule enrichment.
- Primary constraint = strict EU data residency + customer-managed KMS + private connectivity to their GCP VPC.

Attendees:
- Tom Hargreaves (Havenbrook VP Platform)
- Saira Rahman (Lead Data Engineer)
- Jae Park (AI Product)
- Rowan Price (Redwood SE)
- Lina Alvarez (Redwood Solutions)

High-level ask:
1) Real-time chat for agents (latency target 100–200ms per token, p95 <= 400ms) for short turns (avg 80 tokens).
2) Nightly batch scoring job: 1.2M records/day, embeddings + rerank to produce ranked alerts.
3) Auditability: full request/response logging (encrypted), immutable audit trail export monthly.
4) Key management: customer-managed KMS (HSM preferred), BYOK.

Technical notes / gotchas observed:
- Havenbrook currently runs primarily in europe-west1 and uses private interconnect to their on-prem datacenter. They will not permit any egress to public hosted endpoints for PII-containing payloads.
- They have an existing tokenization step in their pipeline that expects whitespace-token counts; we need to validate Redwood token accounting vs their tooling for cost projections.
- Their batch workload wants FP16 quantized models to reduce cost but they are concerned about hallucination risk for regulatory content. Recommend staged evals.
- Auth: internal services use mTLS to a gateway; they asked if Redwood Private can support mTLS between customer-tenant proxies and our inference frontends. Need engineering confirmation.
- Observability: they need per-request trace ids surfaced to their Splunk ingestion. We'll map `redwood_request_id` -> external header.

Model / infra options discussed:
- Hosted private control plane + Private inference nodes inside their VPC (Redwood Private VPC option) seemed preferred.
- For chat: medium Llama-family variant with best-attention kernels + KV cache and prefix caching suggested to meet latency. Consider dynamic batching with strict max batch size 4 for p95 latency.
- For embedding batch: AS256-size quantized model pipeline, GPU spot-friendly autoscaling for nightly window.

Security / Compliance:
- Data residency: logs and artifacts must stay in eu-west1. Confirm cross-region fallback policy is disabled or restricted.
- Retention: they want 7-year archival copies for audit. Need to discuss retention addon pricing.
- Access control: SCIM provisioning + SSO (SAML) for agent accounts.

Immediate action items (owners):
- ROWAN: produce a one-pager with proposed architecture options (Private VPC, Dedicated reserved pool, model variants) by 2024-11-12. (JIRA-INV-1293 linked).
- LINA: validate KMS/HSM integration checklist and confirm if mTLS requirement is supported or if a proxy is needed by 2024-11-13.
- MARCUS: draft cost estimate for the nightly batch (1.2M records/day) including storage/retention and quantization tradeoffs by 2024-11-14.
- SAIRA (Havenbrook): share a sanitized sample of 2k records for model quality evals (privacy-preserving) and their tokenization script by 2024-11-11.

Open questions to clarify with Havenbrook:
- Will they accept our recommended fallbacks (model variant with stronger hallucination mitigations) if the primary quantized model exhibits regressions?
- How strict is the offline export format for audit archives (WORM objects vs signed manifests)?
- Can they provide throughput expectations in RPS for peak agent hours (we only have daily ticket counts now)?

Notes from quick technical probe (from call):
- Saira indicated they have a legacy HSM (Thales) that they want to keep. Need to confirm Redwood Private KMS connector compatibility.
- Jae expressed concern about tokenization mismatch affecting semantic search recall; propose small A/B eval comparing our sentencepiece vs their whitespace pipeline.

Suggested next steps for next call:
- Walk through architecture one-pager and map out network path for private connectivity (we should have network diagrams).
- Agree on a minimal eval plan: 2k sanitized records -> embeddings + rerank -> human review for precision at top-10.
- Confirm provisioning timeline for a 30-day private pilot (scope: chat + nightly batch).

Quick wins to propose in pilot:
- Prefix caching for common inquiry templates to shave p95 latency.
- Short-term fallback policy: route to smaller hosted model for non-PII requests to reduce cost.

Misc scratch notes (internal):
- Cost note: if embeddings are batched and quantized we estimate per-embedding cost ~ 0.0009 USD (rough). Recalculate after Marcus's estimate.
- Risk: regulatory teams will ask for provenance of training data for model variant. Prep an explanation of data sources for chosen model.

Bottom line: Havenbrook is a medium-risk, high-value pilot (strong security needs). Prioritize KMS + private connectivity proof points. Keep this doc as canonical intake notes until we produce the architecture brief.
